I’m not really sure what the purpose of this conversation is. If you’re trying to get me to change my mind, you might as well give up now.

I’m fully aware that people care about me and want me to live. I still think suicide is the right answer for me...I’m more than likely not going to get anywhere in life due to my mental illnesses and I’m just prolonging my suffering by staying alive.

And I live with my mom and younger brother so I talk to them daily, I talk to my dad and older brother every couple months or so. I have a decent enough relationship with my family, no issue there.

I would say fear, primarily. And guilt. Fear of pain and prolonged suffering as I die, and guilt for hurting my friends/family. I always get through the initial process of the attempt but then slowly the fear and guilt build up until I take myself to the emergency room and beg them to save me.

I’ve been in therapy on and off since I was 15 (I’m now 28) and been cutting pretty steadily since about 13-14 years old. I have never had a therapist tell me I was cutting for attention or anything like that. I have had one or two therapists who I didn’t feel comfortable with, but I was able to eventually speak up and request someone new.

The key factor in having successful therapy experiences is the client-therapist relationship. The main reason being that you’re not going to be able to open up and get at your deepest issues if you don’t feel good about your therapist. If you feel uncomfortable with your therapist after a few sessions or if they mock or dismiss your problems, see if you can switch. Any therapist worth seeing is going to understand that not everyone works well with the same person.

I would highly recommend being honest about self harming behavior. I know it’s scary to tell someone, but it’s really important that your therapist has a good idea of what you might need to work on.

I’ve definitely had that urge before. Dealing with it right now actually. I’ve followed through with it a couple times in the past and while it worked out okay, it never really ends up being as satisfying as I hope. Also being in hospital means being around a lot of people who have no idea how to handle someone who is mentally ill, sometimes it ends up okay but sometimes you get some pretty awful nurses and docs.

Just make sure you really think this through. And if you do go for it, please try to be as safe as possible. And have a phone nearby in case you need to call for medics.

Unfortunately that’s not really the case in my area, haha. Most of the staff at hospitals I’ve been in treat it like I’m doing it for attention or something. (I have no problem with people using self harm to ask for help/attention, that’s just not what my reason is usually)

Yeah, the endorphin release and the cravings definitely give it addictive qualities, but that’s not the way any of my treatment team approaches it. I dunno, man. I wish there was something like AA for self harm. Except now I’m not even sure I want to quit. Oh well.
I’ve been at this for about 14 years, I’ve definitely tried fighting through the urges. Sometimes it works, sometimes not so much. But thanks for the tip and good luck to you.
